segments: The 17th dynasty.

beginning with Eljigidey Noyan,
the one whom Güyük Khan had appointed over the West,
they began,
and all the others who were with him they cast down to the ground.
And he also sent and brought Qadaq Noyan again in a cart,
and after he confessed his folly,
he was killed miserably.
Likewise also the wife of Güyük Khan, when they judged her,
they killed her.
Her sons, however, out of respect for the royal lineage, he did not kill,
but to each one he ordered that they should dwell in a specific place,
along with a few people who would serve them.
And thus the kingdom was firmly established for Möngke Khan.
And to his brother Kublai the countries of the Chinese,
who are the Cathayans,
he entrusted.
And to his other brother, who was Hulagu, he sent to the countries of the West {OCR?}.
And the youngest, whose name was Ariq Böke, he kept in his presence.
And he established a law that in the countries of the Cathayans,
every wealthy man should give fifteen gold dinars in tax each year,
and a poor man one dinar;
and in Persia:
every wealthy man ten dinars,
and a poor man one dinar.
And from livestock he ordered
that from every hundred head, one head should be taken;
and from whoever possessed fewer than a hundred,
nothing should be taken.
And for all the bound and imprisoned, he appointed release from distress.
And the pagan priests together with the priests, deacons, monks, and Muslim scholars, he commanded to be exempt {OCR?} from taxes;
and among all the nations, only the Jews were excluded from this favor.
And concerning them at that time a poet said:
"In this freedom, O Jew, you have no share;
except for contempt, O wretched one, you have no companion."
And in this very year,
which is the year 1562,
1562 of the Greeks,
a division fell among the Turkish slaves (Mamluks) of Egypt.
And some of them sent to al-Malik al-Nasir while he reigned in Damascus,
and urged him to enter Egypt and they would deliver it to him.
And al-Malik al-Nasir gathered a large force,
and went to Gaza in order to enter and reign over Egypt.
And when those Turks who were not pleased with him heard,
they gathered their own army.
And they also brought out a great number of the Franks who were imprisoned with them,
